scope: Six-theme archive interpretation and its 19-post evidence companion

human_roles.human: Ian G. Williams defined the cohort-trend and archive-exploration objectives.

Ian G. Williams requested academic-year cohort comparisons, NLTK/MALLET analysis, and a body-credit re-audit. Implementation details were agent-developed. Ian requested two simulated reviewer perspectives and incorporation of the additional persona review, then prioritized research/examination use. Ian requested the theme-oriented visualization revision; the evidence layers and counting definitions were operationalized by the agent.

Ian G. Williams set priorities through successive requests and revisions. Ian designated a public correction contact and retained licensing decisions. Ian selected the project title and authorized a private GCDigitalFellows repository under the authenticated perlsdiver account. Ian authorized public website publishing while keeping the source repository private.
Ian G. Williams supplied the WordPress XML export. Source writers’ contributions are acknowledged separately below. Ian supplied TTT-Website-review.md and the public contact details.
Ian G. Williams directed the work and requested corrections; this does not establish line-by-line human review of all outputs.

Ian G. Williams identified missing authors and required re-analysis. Numerical tests and browser checks were agent-run; independent human replication is not documented. Ian identified the incorrect account attribution for Linked Data for the Uninitiated (Part 1), named McMichael, and requested this archive-wide correction.

Ian G. Williams requested clearer explanations, human-readable annotations, and attribution corrections. Human rewriting of every passage is not claimed. Ian authorized implementation of the review recommendations; this is not confirmation of every resulting claim.

role_confirmation: Evidence-based project mapping; contributor confirmation of individual roles and final approval of this essay are not recorded.
delegator: Ian G. Williams, through requests for source-linked interpretation, website integration and attribution revision
ai_tool: OpenAI Codex (OpenAI); exact underlying model/build not recorded in project artifacts

ai_tasks.work: Two Codex sub-agents inspected the site; Codex also assessed the external persona review identified by Ian as Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017 in the CAIL sandbox in OpenWebUI, using a previous-iteration ZIP. These were not human reviews.
Synthesized the review findings and proposed/implemented a research-first revision plan with explicitly unresolved human decisions.
Selected 19 posts, joined corrected author credits and organized the source ledger.
Checked selected passages against the XML; these were agent-run checks, not independent human verification.
Proposed the six themes and their interpretive connections; no new statistical finding was computed.
Drafted the essay and explanatory attribution text.
Revised wording and attribution disclosure in response to the requester.
Built the source-evidence companion and website interpretation tab.
Documented selection, attribution, access and causal-inference limits; this taxonomy heading does not make AI a human supervisor.

human_review_limit: Project direction and critical feedback are documented. Human passage-by-passage verification, independent replication and approval of all conclusions are not established.
source_writer_boundary: Source writers are credited at each cited post. They are not assigned CRediT roles in this new interpretation; their endorsement and historical AI use are not assessed.
computation_boundary: The revised interpretation includes a targeted reading of five additional posts from 2018–2022 after simulated AI review. No NLTK/MALLET refit was performed. Existing software outputs are separate from the generative-AI interpretation.
